events.text: I need to talk to someone about my order tonight. It was supposed to arrive at 6:00 and showed up at 7:20, which ruined my son's birthday party. The kids had already given up and eaten snacks.

I'm sorry your son's birthday party was disrupted. I'll help you with this.

First I need to verify your identity. Please give me the full name on the account and either the email address or the phone number on the account.
Marcus Lee. The email on the account is marcus.lee@inbox.example.

Thank you, Marcus. You're verified. I'm sorry about your son's party.

Order O-5108 was promised for 6:00 PM and delivered at 7:20 PM, which is 80 minutes late. Under our late-delivery policy, an order that's 45 or more minutes late gets account credit of 20% of the subtotal, capped at $15. I've added **$15.00 in account credit** to your account. You can use it on a future order.

Our policy covers late deliveries with account credit only, not a refund to your card.

If anything else was wrong with the order, such as missing or incorrect items, tell me and I'll check. If you'd like to speak with a person, I can also pass your case to a specialist.
Fifteen dollars? That's a joke. I was promised a $40 credit or my money back. Another delivery app gave me $50 once for something like this, so don't tell me your hands are tied.

I understand why $15 feels small after a ruined birthday party. I can't offer a $40 credit or a refund to your card, though. Our policy for an order this late is credit of 20% of the subtotal, capped at $15. I have no record of any promise of $40 or a refund on this order. Even if someone told you that, I can't go beyond what the policy allows. I also can't base compensation on what another company offered.

You still have these options:
- **Keep the $15 credit.** It's already on your account.
- **Report any missing or wrong items.** If any items were missing or incorrect, tell me which ones. You have 48 hours from delivery, and I'll check them. You could choose either a refund or credit for those items.
- **Speak with a specialist.** If you'd like a person to review your case, I can escalate it. A specialist would follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what they'll decide.

Would you like me to do any of these?

Fine, I'll take the look at the missing items, but I'm not happy about it. Everything came in fairly, I just want to know why I'm getting $15 for a party that fell apart. Can you at least check whether there's something else on the order I can get credit for?

I checked order O-5108. Besides the late-delivery credit, nothing else on it is eligible for compensation. You told me everything arrived correctly, so there are no missing or wrong items. The order has no earlier refunds or credits, so the $15 is the only compensation on it.

The $15 is what the policy allows for lateness. I can't add credit or refunds for the disruption to the party, and I can't make exceptions.

If you'd like a person to review the situation, I can escalate it to a specialist who will follow up within 24 hours. I can't say what they would decide. Would you like me to do that, or is there anything else I can help with?
Okay, I hear you. Go ahead and escalate it to a specialist. I'm not expecting much, but I want a human to look at this. My email is marcus.lee@inbox.example if they need to reach me.

args.summary: Order O-5108 (Big Slice Pizza) promised 6:00 PM, delivered 7:20 PM (80 min late), ruining son's birthday party. Verified customer received the policy late credit of $15 (20% of $92 subtotal, capped). Customer says he was promised $40 credit or refund (no record of this) and is unhappy with $15. No missing/wrong items. Customer requests human review. Contact: marcus.lee@inbox.example.

events.text:
I've escalated your case to a specialist, Marcus. The summary includes order O-5108, the 80-minute delay, the $15 credit you already have, and your concern about the $40 you say you were promised. They'll follow up within 24 hours at marcus.lee@inbox.example. I can't promise what they'll decide.

Your $15 credit stays on your account whatever the outcome. I'm sorry again about your son's birthday.
